item.title: Hawk Fire evacuations in Reno slightly eased as firefighters make gains
item.description: Shifting winds challenged firefighters battling the Hawk Fire in Reno, Nevada, that was keeping tens of thousands of people evacuated.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy trial judge denies mistrial request, reprimands prosecution
item.description: Lindsay Clancy trial testimony ended abruptly Monday in Plymouth Superior Court when a witness began speaking about religion and the defense unsuccessfully called for a mistrial.

item.title: How the Robot Games are going in Beijing
item.description: The World Humanoid Robot Games are underway in Beijing, China, in a stadium repurposed from the 2022 Winter Olympics. Many of the machines on display can now outrun and out-jump even the best real-life Olympians. Anna Coren has the story.

item.title: 49ers owner arrested in police setup
item.description: The owner of the San Francisco 49ers was arrested this weekend at a trailer park, allegedly there to pay $140 for sex in what turned out to be a police setup. Carter Evans reports.

item.title: Why Trump's Canada tariffs are likely to have a modest impact on prices
item.description: Although some Canadian goods will get more expensive in the U.S., trade experts don't expect a broader inflation spike.

item.title: Trump announces 50% tariffs on Canadian automotive and steel imports
item.description: President Trump said tariffs on Canadian automotive and steel imports will rise to 50% on Jan. 1, 2027, in a social media post.

item.title: 23-year-old pilot pulls off crash landing near busy Florida beach
item.description: Dramatic video captured a 23-year-old pilot's small plane in trouble, landing off the coast of Boca Raton, Florida. Kris Van Cleave reports.

item.title: Trade war of words intensifies between U.S., Canada
item.description: The Trump administration announced its so-called "economic D-Day" plans against Iran on Monday, while also lashing out at Canada and threatening more tariffs. Nancy Cordes has more details on this and a new Supreme Court ruling backing Trump's order to limit mail-in ballots.

item.title: Mystery under the streets of New York City as 3 people emerge from manhole
item.description: Video captured three people wearing headlamps and rubber overalls emerging from a manhole in New York City last week during the overnight hours. This is at least the third such sighting, and police cannot fully explain it. Tom Hanson has more details.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy defense calls for mistrial after witness brings up Clancy's Catholic faith
item.description: Closing arguments are expected this week in the murder case of Lindsay Clancy. The defense called for a mistrial on Monday after a prosecution witness brought up Clancy's Catholic faith and the concept of mortal sin. Shanelle Kaul has more details from the courthouse.

item.title: Rush to escape in Nevada as Hawk Fire sweeps into Reno neighborhoods
item.description: Authorities in Nevada told tens of thousands of people to evacuate ahead of a fast-moving wildfire on Monday. Jason Allen reports from the scene.

item.title: Darline Graham says she's focusing on affordability, doesn't offer up plan a day before runoff
item.description: Republican voters in South Carolina will head to the polls Tuesday in their state's special Senate primary runoff between Darline Graham and Ralph Norman. CBS News senior White House and political correspondent Ed O'Keefe has more.

item.title: Sailor on USS Lincoln says dad detained by immigration officials
item.description: A sailor on the USS Lincoln says his dad was arrested by immigration officials. CBS News immigration correspondent Camilo Montoya-Galvez has more.

item.title: What to know as U.S. announces "Operation Economic Outcast" campaign to cripple Iran's economy
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday laid out the Trump administration's plan for a campaign to create "economic onslaught" against Iran and its partners. "Face the Nation" coordinating producer Richard Escobedo has more.

item.title: Latest on Lindsay Clancy trial as judge denies mistrial request
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's defense team asked for a mistrial Monday after a witness began speaking about Catholic religion. The judge in the case denied the request. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul has more.

item.title: Supreme Court allows Trump to implement parts of order restricting mail voting
item.description: The Supreme Court divided 6-3 in granting the Trump administration's request for emergency relief.

item.title: Kushner and Jeffries held private meeting, New York Times reports
item.description: According to The New York Times, House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries recently held a private meeting with President Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner. Political strategists Joel Payne and Todd Ricketts join with analysis.

item.title: Retired U.S. Army major shares life lessons from 20 near-death experiences
item.description: Urban warfare expert and Ret. U.S. Army Maj. John Spencer is sharing life lessons he learned from his many near-death experiences in a new book titled "20 Times I Almost Died." Spencer joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: How this summer's food recalls compare to past years
item.description: It feels like there's been a new food recall every week this summer, but former FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb says the number of recalls has been on par with other years. CBS News medical correspondent Dr. Céline Gounder joins "The Takeout" with more.

item.title: Former Stars and Stripes editor-in-chief says his firing "was a real shock"
item.description: The Pentagon has terminated several staff members of the military newspaper "Stars and Stripes" for alleged insubordination. Former Editor-In-Chief Erik Slavin says he was removed because of an interview he gave to "CBS Sunday Morning" about censorship. Slavin joins "The Takeout" to discuss his removal.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy trial judge tells jurors to disregard religious testimony
item.description: Defense attorneys for Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts mother who admitted to killing her children, called for a mistrial on Monday, citing a witness who used the phrase "moral sin." The judge denied the request. CBS News correspondent Shanelle Kaul reports.

item.title: Bessent offers scant details about "economic D-Day" sanctions against Iran
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday announced the U.S. is launching an "economic onslaught" against Iran and its partners, but did not give details on who might be sanctioned. CBS News' Nancy Cordes and Aaron MacLean have the latest.

item.title: Supreme Court lets Trump's order overhauling mail-in voting take effect for now
item.description: The Supreme Court on Monday allowed President Trump's executive order targeting mail-in voting to take effect while legal challenges play out. CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson breaks down the procedural decision.

item.title: Gen Xers fret over Social Security. "I will likely be working in retirement."
item.description: Millions of Generation X Americans expect to depend on Social Security as their main — or only — source of retirement income.

item.title: Body of wife wanted in Worcester, Massachusetts, police officer's death found
item.description: Karen Solomon​, wanted for questioning in the death of her Worcester, Massachusetts, police officer​ husband, has been found dead after a massive search.

item.title: Nearly 25% of workers are "functionally unemployed," analysis finds
item.description: An alternative measure of unemployment that accounts for wages suggests the U.S. labor market is weaker than it looks.

item.title: Women left behind in high-paying AI job boom, LinkedIn research finds
item.description: While hiring for AI companies is booming, women are getting left behind, according to new research from LinkedIn. It found that female candidates accounted for 26% of hires for jobs requiring AI skills in the U.S., compared to 50% of women hired into non-AI positions. Sarah Steinberg, the head of global public policy partnerships at LinkedIn, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Breaking down Scott Bessent's comments on Canada, tariffs, Mark Carney
item.description: The U.S. is imposing a 50% tariff on $20 billion in Canadian goods. Canada vowed to retaliate with tariffs of their own that would go into effect on Sept. 8. Rob Russo, a Canadian correspondent for The Economist, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Massachusetts woman suspected of killing husband found dead
item.description: Karen Solomon, a Massachusetts woman wanted for questioning in the death of her police officer husband, has been found dead, Worcester authorities announced on Monday. Law enforcement called the case a "tragic murder-suicide."

item.title: Bessent announces campaign to create "economic onslaught" against Iran and its partners
item.description: The Trump administration is trying to pull all economic levers at its disposal to cripple Tehran.
